THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO ISSUE THE WRIT OF CERTIORARI TO QUASH THE ORDER NO.AC/KSHIP/27A/30/2014- 15/155 DATED:28.10.2016 PASSED BY THE 1ST RESPONDENT THE COPY WHICH HAS BEEN PRODUCED HEREWITH AND MARKED AS ANNEXURE-A; ISSUE A WRIT OF MANDAMUS DIRECTING THE 1ST RESPONDENT TO REFER THE MATTER TO THE COMPETENT CIVIL COURT FOR DETERMINATION OF THE AMOUNT OF COMPENSATION PAYABLE TO THE PETITIONERS UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE KARNATAKA STATE HIGHWAYS ACT 1964 ALONG WITH THE APPLICATIONS FILED BY THE PETITIONERS AS PER ANNEXURE-B TO E.
 THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER The captioned petition is filed by the land losers feeling aggrieved by the order passed by respondent No.1- Assistant Commissioner vide Annexure-A.
2.
Brief facts leading to the filing of the case are that, petitioners land was acquired under the provisions of Karnataka State Highways Act, 1964 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short).
The subject matter of petitioners residential site has NA potentiality.
As the petitioners were not willing to accept the offer made by respondent No.1- Assistant Commissioner, a general award was passed under Section 28 of the Act on 27.09.2014.

Petitioners however claim that no notice or award was issued to the NC: 2023:KHC-D:8762 petitioners and it was only on deposit of the amount in the civil court and an intimation by the civil court, the petitioners came to know about passing of the award.

Having gained the knowledge, petitioners immediately filed an application under Section 35(1)
seeking reference to enable the petitioners to seek higher compensation before the civil court.
The petitioners along with reference application also filed an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

Respondent No.1- Assistant Commissioner vide impugned order has rejected the reference application on the ground that he has no jurisdiction to entertain the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
The said order is under challenge.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AGA for the respondents.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The order under challenge is cryptic and rejection of reference application on the ground that he has no jurisdiction to entertain the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act is perverse and contrary to NC: 2023:KHC-D:8762 sub-section (3) of Section 35 of the Act.
Under Karnataka Highways Act, 1964, though an application for reference is to be made within six weeks from the date of the award, land looser has the benefit of Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
Without taking note of these relevant provisions, respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner has rejected the application which has lead to miscarriage of justice.
Petitioners having lost valuable residential site have been left remediless on account of cryptic order passed by respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner.
5. The next question that requires consideration is, whether respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner has jurisdiction to pass the order on an application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
Even that aspect is not dealt by respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner.

6. In the light of the discussion made supra, I pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:8762 ii) The impugned order dated passed by respondent No.1- Assistant Commissioner is hereby set aside.
Respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner shall look into the provisions of Section 35 and thereafter proceed to pass appropriate order.

iii) Respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner is also required to examine as to whether he has any authority to pass order on an application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act or that, he is required to remit the reference application along with application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

iv) Since the reference application is returned by respondent No.1-Assistant Commissioner,
petitioner is reserved with liberty to present the reference application along with earlier application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

Sd/-
